summary: Customer SDK keepalive coalescing causing autoscaler under-provisioning and transient GPU shortages
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-09 08:30 UTC AcmeAnalytics reported recurring transient throughput drops on their dedicated pool in us-west. Symptoms looked like sudden p99/p50 increases and a queued backlog followed by short GPU attach failures. This started after a customer deploy of an updated analytics SDK that batches/ coalesces TCP keepalive/heartbeat emissions in low-traffic periods.

Impact: Several customer routes experienced ~30-40% throughput degradation for 10-25 minute windows during midday traffic, resulting in increased latency for end users and triggering customer SLA alerts. No data loss observed; requests were delayed and occasionally routed to fallback (smaller) variants.

Environment: prod us-west (Acme dedicated pool: reserve-id: dp-usw-acme-22). Autoscaler SLOs configured at p95 attach latency 350ms and target utilization 70%.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Deploy SDK v2.7.1 configured with keepalive_coalesce=true and keepalive_compress_window=30s.
2) Simulate low steady background connections plus periodic bursts from analytics pipeline.
3) Observe autoscaler (predictive) failing to add capacity quickly; GPU attach lag grows and queued-batch backlog forms.
investigation:
Timeline and observations:
- 2026-03-09 08:35 UTC: Support received first alert from customer (CS).
- 08:40 UTC: SRE pulled autoscaler metrics (grafana/dedicated/autoscale-usw) — increase in attach_latency and a delayed increase in desired_replicas compared to request rate.
- 08:45 UTC: Noted sparse telemetry from tenant heartbeat stream: connection_count and keepalive_emit metrics were coalesced into infrequent bursts.
- 08:50 UTC: Checked network/tls logs — no packet loss. NVLink and GPU telemetry normal.
- 09:00 UTC: Correlated with customer-deployed SDK release (AcmeAnalytics / analytics-sdk v2.7.1) which introduced keepalive coalescing to reduce CPU on clients.

Hypothesis: The autoscaler relies on frequent low-level connection heartbeats/telemetry to infer active warm connections and to trigger predictive pre-warm actions. The customer's SDK coalescing suppressed heartbeat emission during quiet periods; autoscaler sampling windows undercounted active warm slots and delayed replica increases. When the burst arrived, the autoscaler reacted late, causing transient GPU attach pressure, slot scarcity and effective noisy-neighbor symptoms (other tenants' prefetch/kv-cache got preempted).

Data collected and links:
- Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/dedicated-autoscale-usw?from=2026-03-09T08:00:00Z&to=2026-03-09T10:00:00Z
- Customer SDK commit: github.com/acme/analytics-sdk@c7b2a4f
- Slack thread: #support-acme thread id: tXc9b34
- Kernel logs for GPU attach spikes: s3://redwood-logs/dedicated/us-west/2026-03-09/attach-spikes.log

Partial findings:
- Autoscaler sampling window of 60s combined with client coalescing windows of 30s resulted in systematic undercounting during common traffic patterns.
- When bursts occurred, backlog grew faster than autoscaler could provision GPUs given current cooldown/hysteresis settings.
- Some neighboring tenants experienced KV-cache evictions (observed on console) coincident with attach pressure which amplified perceived noisy-neighbor behaviour.

Next steps in investigation:
- SRE to replay metrics with synthetic coalesced heartbeats to reproduce undercounting locally (assigned to Marco).
- Request customer to temporarily disable keepalive_coalesce to validate correlation (customer prompted 2026-03-09 09:15).
- Engineering to evaluate autoscaler sampling sensitivity and predictive model to tolerate coalesced telemetry (follow-up PR).

resolution:
Mitigation applied:
- Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-09): instructed AcmeAnalytics to disable keepalive_coalesce in their SDK; they confirmed immediate improvement.
- Short-term platform fix: lowered autoscaler sampling window to 30s for affected dedicated pools and reduced cooldown from 2m to 45s for predictive path to be more responsive to sudden bursts (canary rolled 2026-03-11).

Longer-term remediation:
1) Autoscaler: engineering to add detection for telemetry coalescing (detect low-variance heartbeat patterns) and switch predictive estimator to rely more on external traffic proxies rather than heartbeats. Target: design doc by 2026-03-20, implementation Q2. (Owner: Autoscale team).
2) SDK guidance: update customer-facing docs recommending keepalive_coalesce=false for dedicated pools or provide guidance on config values compatible with Redwood autoscaler sampling windows. Opened PR in acme repo for doc update.
3) Postmortem: schedule 72-hour postmortem with SRE/Product/Customer success to align on monitoring, alerting adjustments and customer onboarding checklist for dedicated deployments.

Status: Customer returned to baseline. Follow-ups scheduled and owner assignments documented. Incident remains open while autoscaler PR is in review.
